original_test_intent: Inject a synthetic PMIC high-temperature warning for every required DIMM sensor, verify exactly one correctable warning assertion without critical shutdown or reset, then verify deassertion/clear and continued memory, fan and thermal-control health.
original_method: Map each PMIC temperature sensor and I2C address; prove railtype8 and valid parameters; resolve severity; record actual temperature and warning/critical thresholds; inject one synthetic warning while physical temperature remains safe; correlate assert event and no critical status; clear/deassert by approved semantics; verify OS/BMC/fan/memory health; restore settings before another sensor.
manual_activity: The thermal/PMIC owner resolves the warning stimulus and target sensor, supervises a synthetic assertion, confirms no critical action, clears/deasserts the warning and restores PMIC/I2C state.
required_inputs: Vendor proof railtype8 selects High Temperature Warning and whether voltagetype0/1 is applicable
Decision on Fatal step label versus correctable warning severity and explicit no-reset/no-shutdown rule
Warning threshold, critical threshold, hysteresis, latch and clear/deassert semantics
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/OOB path and expected warning status response
Fresh PMIC/CPER/SEL assert/deassert fields, OS timeout, fan/memory health, aborts and restoration
safety_requirements: Synthetic injection only; do not heat the DIMM/PMIC
Independent actual-temperature, fan, power and OOB monitoring with margin below critical threshold
One mapped sensor once; require exactly one warning, no critical bit/power action and approved deassert before another
Abort on real temperature rise, critical status, shutdown/reset, fan anomaly, DIMM error, wrong sensor or I2C loss
No automatic clear/retry/loop; restore PMIC mode, SPD ownership, telemetry, I2C and HDT and confirm normal sensors
agent_execution_scope: Validate warning register/threshold, sensor/I2C matrix, severity, assert/deassert and recovery plan
Collect read-only actual temperatures, warning/critical status, OS/CPER/SEL, fan and memory health
Do not heat, infer parameters, alter PMIC/I2C/BIOS/HDT, inject, clear, repeat, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve sensor matrix, thresholds and synthetic stimulus
Restore state and issue per-sensor verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The step is labeled Fatal while Items and Criteria describe a correctable warning, with no no-reset/no-shutdown rule. Voltage types0/1 are applied to a thermal threshold without semantics, one fixed tuple is used for all DIMMs, and threshold/hysteresis/assert/deassert criteria are absent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The synthetic high-temperature warning purpose is identifiable. Engineering can resolve severity, parameters and sensor mapping, so static review completes without physical heating.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 96 Wistron-System RAS-00816-V002: prove railtype8 is High Temperature Warning and decide whether voltagetype0/1 applies; reconcile Fatal step label with correctable warning and define no-reset/no-shutdown; specify warning/critical thresholds, hysteresis, latch/clear/assert/deassert and no-real-heating limits; map every DIMM/PMIC sensor plus Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path; approve tuple matrix, PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence, OS timeout, fan/memory recovery, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Defines a safe synthetic warning transition with exact assertion, negative critical action and deassertion evidence rather than generic temperature logging.
independent_technical_reasoning: A warning test passes only if the warning state asserts at the intended synthetic threshold while the critical-shutdown path remains inactive. The source's Fatal wording and voltage-type loop look inherited from other PMIC cases and cannot determine the behavior. Physical temperature must stay safely below critical, and the status must deassert or clear by a documented method so a stale warning cannot satisfy later targets.
